Actually, I recall that in this faiss version, HNSW search had something like:

std::vector<SearchContext> contexts(omp_get_max_threads());

allocated per search call, with each thread indexing by its thread number within the parallel region. Not thread-id keyed. So the "per search call" pattern is the Faiss idiom: allocate scratch per search() call, and if parallelizing within a call, each worker gets its own slot. Since we process queries sequentially (first version), one scratch per search() call suffices. Per-call cost: S (MB floats = 8KB), Q (2KB), P (64B), visited (N4 = 4MB for N=1M).

Hmm, 4MB allocation + zero-init per call. For an interactive use case of 1 query per call — that's the cost. The generation counter doesn't help across calls if we re-allocate per call. Alternative: cache the visited buffer keyed by (thread::id) to amortize across calls on the same thread.

Let's go with a thread-id-keyed cache:

  • Per-search call: look up/create ThreadState for std::this_thread::get_id() (protected by mutex, released before the actual work).
  • ThreadState holds visited + generation + other scratch.
  • Memory grows per distinct thread that searches. To bound it: when the number of cached states exceeds some threshold (e.g., 4× omp_get_max_threads() + a few), evict the oldest / least-recently-used? Complicated. Or just document: "Each thread that searches this index holds a per-thread scratch buffer (4 * ntotal bytes); long-lived thread pools are assumed."

Hmm. Actually, let me reconsider: how bad is per-call allocation really? 4MB zero-init ≈ sub-millisecond (memset runs at ~10GB/s → 0.4ms). malloc of 4MB ≈ 10-50µs. Acceptable as a first version; and "reuse per-query scratch buffers where safe" — safe reuse across queries within a call via the generation counter. Per-call allocation is thread-safe by construction.

But wait — the task explicitly says: "avoid allocating and clearing an N-sized boolean array per query" — per query, and we satisfy that (per call, with the generation trick within a call). And "visited state must be query-local or thread-local. Never share mutable dedup state across concurrent searches." Per-call local = query-local in the sequential first version.

Decision: hybrid — a small per-thread cache with a size cap:

  • std::unordered_map<std::thread::id, std::shared_ptr<ThreadState>> under a mutex.
  • Cap: if the map size exceeds max(8, 2 * omp_get_max_threads()), remove a random/oldest entry before inserting. LRU-ish: keep an last_used tick counter and evict the one with the smallest tick. Simple enough.

Actually, you know what — simpler and cleaner: use shared_ptr and just evict when the cap is exceeded (no LRU tracking: iterate and erase the first entry). The map preserves insertion order, so erase the begin() entry = oldest thread. A thread's state, once evicted, gets re-created (with re-zeroing visited). Good compromise.

void IndexRecJPQPrune::search(n, x, k, distances, labels, params) const {
    const SearchParametersRecJPQPrune* p = dynamic_cast<const SearchParametersRecJPQPrune*>(params);
    // Validate params
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(k >= 0);
    // Resolve effective parameters
    size_t bs = p ? p->batch_size : batch_size;
    int64_t max_iter = p ? p->max_iterations : max_iterations;
    float infl = p ? p->ub_inflation : ub_inflation;
    bool exact = p ? p->exact_mode : exact_mode;
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(bs >= 1);
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(exact ? (infl == 1.0f) : (infl >= 1.0f));
    if (exact) max_iter = -1;  // unlimited in exact mode
    
    ThreadState& ts = get_thread_state();
    
    for (idx_t qi = 0; qi < n; qi++) {
        bool complete = search_one(qi, x, k, distances, labels, ts, bs, max_iter, infl, exact);
        last_search_complete &= complete; // hmm, last_search_complete is per-call
    }
}

void IndexRecJPQPrune::compute_sub_item_scores(const float* xq, float* S) const {
    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {
        cblas_sgemv(
            CblasRowMajor, CblasNoTrans,
            d_split, B,
            1.0f,
            codebooks.data() + m * B * d_split,
            B,           // lda (row stride)
            xq + m * d_split,
            1,
            0.0f,
            S + m * B,
            B);  // hmm — ldc: S is row-major [M][B]; we want S[m][0..B] → ldc = B, and S + m*B. But wait: sgemv computes y = alpha*A*x + beta*y, where A is m×n…
    }
}

Careful with cblas_sgemv semantics (row-major, no-trans): A is m×n, x is n, y is m. We want: S_row[m][b] = dot(codebook_row[(m,b)], phi_m) — that is, for split m: S_m (1×B) = codebook_m (B×d_split) × phi_m (d_split×1). So A = codebook_m as B×d_split (m=B, n=d_split), x = phi_m, y = S_m (B). cblas_sgemv(CblasRowMajor, CblasNoTrans, m=B, n=d_split, alpha=1, A=codebook_m, lda=d_split, x=phi_m, incx=1, beta=0, y=S_m, incy=1). ✓ Matches the ProductQuantizer::compute_LUT pattern.

void Index::reconstruct_batch(idx_t n, const idx_t* keys, float* recons) const {
    std::mutex exception_mutex;
    std::string exception_string;
#pragma omp parallel for if (n > 1000)
    for (idx_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        try {
            reconstruct(keys[i], &recons[i * d]);
        } catch (const std::exception& e) {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(exception_mutex);
            exception_string = e.what();
        }
    }
    if (!exception_string.empty()) {
        FAISS_THROW_MSG(exception_string.c_str());
    }
}

void Index::reconstruct_n(idx_t i0, idx_t ni, float* recons) const {
#pragma omp parallel for if (ni > 1000)
    for (idx_t i = 0; i < ni; i++) {
        reconstruct(i0 + i, recons + i * d);
    }
}

/*

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include <faiss/Index.h>

namespace faiss {

/** CSR (compressed sparse row) inverted lists for IndexRecJPQPrune.
 *
 * The catalogue of N items is represented by a matrix of N*M item codes;
 * code m of item i is in [0, B).  There are M * B posting lists, identified
 * by
 *
 *     list_id = split * B + sub_item_id
 *
 * Posting list (split, sub_item_id) contains the internal positions of all
 * items whose code at that split equals sub_item_id.
 *
 * Storage is CSR-style:
 *
 *     offsets has M * B + 1 entries;
 *     list items are item_ids[offsets[list_id] .. offsets[list_id + 1]).
 *
 * The storage is dense and unpadded: no entry is reserved for empty posting
 * lists and there is at most one heap allocation for all list contents
 * (plus one for the offsets). Item positions are stored in ascending order
 * (the order in which items were added), which makes postings lists
 * amenable to sequential access.
 */
struct RecJPQInvertedLists {
    size_t M = 0; ///< number of splits
    size_t B = 0; ///< number of sub-item ids per split

    /** offsets of the M * B + 1 posting list boundaries */
    std::vector<size_t> offsets;
    /** concatenation of all posting lists: total of N * M entries */
    std::vector<idx_t> item_ids;

    /** Two-pass construction from a row-major N x M uint8 code matrix.
     *
     * @param item_codes  N * M codes, code m of item i at [i * M + m], in [0, B)
     * @param N           number of items
     * @param M           number of splits
     * @param B           number of sub-item ids per split
     */
    void build(const uint8_t* item_codes, size_t N, size_t M, size_t B);

    /** Drop all postings. */
    void clear();

    /// number of items in the posting list (split, sub_item_id)
    size_t list_size(size_t split, size_t sub_item_id) const;

    /// pointer to the first entry of the posting list
    const idx_t* get_list(size_t split, size_t sub_item_id) const;

    /// half-open range [begin, end) of the posting list contents
    std::pair<const idx_t*, const idx_t*> get_list_range(
            size_t split,
            size_t sub_item_id) const;

    /// total number of postings (N * M after build)
    size_t total_entries() const {
        return item_ids.size();
    }
};

} // namespace faiss

The .cpp is:

#include <faiss/invlists/RecJPQInvertedLists.h>

#include <faiss/impl/FaissAssert.h>

#include <algorithm>

namespace faiss {

void RecJPQInvertedLists::build(
        const uint8_t* item_codes,
        size_t N,
        size_t M,
        size_t B) {
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(M >= 1, "RecJPQInvertedLists: M must be >= 1");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(B >= 1, "RecJPQInvertedLists: B must be >= 1");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(
            B <= 256, "RecJPQInvertedLists: B must be <= 256 (uint8 codes)");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(item_codes != nullptr, "...");

    size_t nlists = M * B;

    // Pass 1: count items per posting list (validates codes on the fly)
    offsets.assign(nlists + 1, 0);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        const uint8_t* c = item_codes + i * M;
        for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {
            FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(
                    c[m] < B,
                    "RecJPQInvertedLists: item %" PRId64
                    " has code %u >= B (%zu) in split %zu",
                    (idx_t)i, c[m], B, m);
            offsets[(m * B + c[m]) + 1]++;
        }
    }
    // Prefix sum: offsets[i+1] -= offsets[i] ... standard
    for (size_t i = 0; i < nlists; i++) {
        offsets[i + 1] += offsets[i];
    }

    // Pass 2: fill contiguous storage, preserving item order
    item_ids.resize(N * M);   // hmm: total entries = N*M
    std::vector<size_t> cursor(offsets.begin(), offsets.end() - 1);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        const uint8_t* c = item_codes + i * M;
        for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {
            item_ids[cursor[m * B + c[m]]++] = (idx_t)i;
        }
    }

    this->M = M;
    this->B = B;
}

void RecJPQInvertedLists::clear() {
    offsets.clear();
    item_ids.clear();
    M = B = 0;
}

size_t RecJPQInvertedLists::list_size(size_t split, size_t sub_item_id) const {
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(split < M && sub_item_id < B);
    size_t id = split * B + sub_item_id;
    return offsets[id + 1] - offsets[id];
}

const idx_t* RecJPQInvertedLists::get_list(
        size_t split,
        size_t sub_item_id) const {
    return &item_ids[offsets[split * B + sub_item_id]];  // hmm: when item_ids is empty → UB
}

Note: when item_ids is empty, &item_ids[0] is UB (well, &empty[0] is technically UB pre-C++11? In C++11 and later, &v[v.size()] is fine, but &v[0] when size==0 is UB... actually the standard says operator[] with pos >= size is UB; pos == size is allowed for &v[size] (one-past-the-end) but v[0] when size is 0 has pos=0 > = size → UB). Guard: return item_ids.empty() ? nullptr : &item_ids[...]. The caller (search) checks list_size first anyway.

/// Statistics collected during a search, for the caller to inspect.
struct RecJPQPruneStats {
    /// number of main-loop iterations executed
    size_t iterations = 0;
    /// number of unique items whose score was computed
    size_t items_scored = 0;
    /// number of posting-list entries visited (before deduplication)
    size_t postings_traversed = 0;
    /// number of sub-item ids processed (batches)
    size_t sub_items_processed = 0;
    /// final value of the sigma upper bound
    float final_sigma = 0;
    /// final value of the theta threshold
    float final_theta = 0;
};

The SearchParameters struct:

struct SearchParametersRecJPQPrune : SearchParameters {
    /// number of sub-item ids processed per main-loop iteration (BS)
    size_t batch_size = 8;
    /// safety limit on main-loop iterations; < 0 means unlimited.
    /// Ignored in exact mode.
    int64_t max_iterations = -1;
    /// multiplier applied to the pruning threshold theta in approximate
    /// mode: search stops as soon as sigma <= theta * ub_inflation.
    /// Must be >= 1.0; 1.0 (default) keeps the search exact.
    float ub_inflation = 1.0f;
    /// when true (default), the search runs until the exact pruning
    /// condition sigma <= theta holds. ub_inflation must be 1.0 and
    /// max_iterations is ignored.
    bool exact_mode = true;
    /// if non-null, filled with per-search statistics
    RecJPQPruneStats* stats = nullptr;
};

struct IndexRecJPQPrune : Index {
    /// number of splits
    size_t M = 0;
    /// number of sub-item ids per split
    size_t B = 0;
    /// dimensionality of one split (d / M)
    size_t d_split = 0;

    /** row-major N * M item codes, code m of item i at [i * M + m] */
    std::vector<uint8_t> item_codes;
    /** external ids, one per item */
    std::vector<idx_t> ids;
    /** codebooks: [M][B][d_split] */
    std::vector<float> codebooks;

    /** CSR inverted lists over the item codes */
    RecJPQInvertedLists invlists;

    /// default search parameters, used when search() gets no params
    size_t batch_size = 8;
    int64_t max_iterations = -1;
    float ub_inflation = 1.0f;
    bool exact_mode = true;

    /// true after the most recent search() call ran to exact termination;
    /// false when an approximate-mode stop (ub_inflation > 1 or the
    /// max_iterations limit) triggered first
    std::atomic<bool> last_search_complete{true};

    /** Construct an empty index.
     *
     * @param d      embedding dimension, a positive multiple of M
     * @param M      number of splits
     * @param B      number of sub-item ids per split, in [1, 256]
     * @param metric must be METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT
     */
    explicit IndexRecJPQPrune(
            size_t d,
            size_t M,
            size_t B,
            MetricType metric = METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT);

    /** Populate the index from RecJPQ codes and codebooks.
     *
     * The index must be empty (call reset() first after a previous build).
     * The supplied arrays are copied; the caller keeps ownership.
     *
     * @param n          number of items
     * @param item_codes N*M uint8 codes, code m of item i at [i*M + m], in [0,B)
     * @param codebooks  M*B*d_split floats: [m][b][j]
     * @param ids        optional external ids, size n; when null the
     *                   sequential ids 0..n-1 are used
     */
    void build(
            size_t n,
            const uint8_t* item_codes,
            const float* codebooks,
            const idx_t* ids = nullptr);

    /** Compute the M x B sub-item score matrix S for query x:
     * S[m][b] = dot(codebooks[m][b], x[m*d_split .. (m+1)*d_split)).
     * This is the PQTopK lookup table, shared by all item scoring. */
    void compute_sub_item_scores(const float* x, float* S) const;

    /** Score a single item given the sub-item score matrix:
     * score(i) = sum_m S[m][item_codes[i*M + m]]. */
    float score_item(size_t i, const float* S) const;

    void add(idx_t n, const float* x) override;
    void add_with_ids(idx_t n, const float* x, const idx_t* xids) override;
    void search(
            idx_t n,
            const float* x,
            idx_t k,
            float* distances,
            idx_t* labels,
            const SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const override;
    void reset() override;
    void reconstruct(idx_t key, float* recons) const override;
    void reconstruct_batch(idx_t n, const idx_t* keys, float* recons) const override;
    void reconstruct_n(idx_t i0, idx_t ni, float* recons) const override;
    /// size in bytes of all data held by the index
    size_t memory_footprint() const;

private:
    ...
};

#include <faiss/IndexRecJPQPrune.h>

#include <faiss/impl/FaissAssert.h>

#include <cblas.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <thread>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>

namespace faiss {

namespace {
constexpr float kNegInf = -std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity();
}

IndexRecJPQPrune::IndexRecJPQPrune(
        size_t d,
        size_t M,
        size_t B,
        MetricType metric)
        : Index(d, metric), M(M), B(B) {
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(d > 0, "IndexRecJPQPrune: d must be > 0");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(M > 0, "IndexRecJPQPrune: M must be > 0");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(B >= 1, "IndexRecJPQPrune: B must be >= 1");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(
            B <= 256,
            "IndexRecJPQPrune: B must be <= 256 (item codes are uint8)");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(
            d % M == 0,
            "IndexRecJPQPrune: d must be a multiple of M");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(
            metric == METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT,
            "IndexRecJPQPrune: only METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT is supported");
    d_split = d / M;
}

build():

void IndexRecJPQPrune::build(
        size_t n,
        const uint8_t* item_codes,
        const float* codebooks,
        const idx_t* ids) {
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(
            ntotal == 0,
            "IndexRecJPQPrune::build: index must be empty (call reset() first)");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(
            item_codes != nullptr, "IndexRecJPQPrune::build: null codes");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(
            codebooks != nullptr, "IndexRecJPQPrune::build: null codebooks");

    size_t n_codebooks = M * B * d_split;
    this->item_codes.assign(item_codes, item_codes + n * M);
    this->codebooks.assign(codebooks, codebooks + n_codebooks);
    if (ids != nullptr) {
        this->ids.assign(ids, ids + n);
    } else {
        this->ids.resize(n);
        std::iota(this->ids.begin(), this->ids.end(), 0);  // hmm idx_t
    }
    // detect sequential ids
    ids_sequential = true;
    for (idx_t i = 0; i < (idx_t)n; i++) {
        if (this->ids[i] != i) {
            ids_sequential = false;
            break;
        }
    }
    invlists.build(this->item_codes.data(), n, M, B);
    ntotal = (idx_t)n;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(id_map_mutex);
        id_to_pos.clear();
        id_map_built = false;
    }
}

compute_sub_item_scores:

void IndexRecJPQPrune::compute_sub_item_scores(
        const float* x,
        float* S) const {
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(
            !codebooks.empty() && codebooks.size() == M * B * d_split);
    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {
        cblas_sgemv(
                CblasRowMajor,
                CblasNoTrans,
                (int)B,
                (int)d_split,
                1.0f,
                codebooks.data() + m * B * d_split,
                (int)d_split,
                x + m * d_split,

float IndexRecJPQPrune::score_item(size_t i, const float* S) const {
    float score = 0.f;
    const uint8_t* c = item_codes.data() + i * M;
    for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {
        score += S[m * B + c[m]];
    }
    return score;
}

void IndexRecJPQPrune::search(
        idx_t n,
        const float* x,
        idx_t k,
        float* distances,
        idx_t* labels,
        const SearchParameters* params) const {
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(k >= 0);
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(
            metric_type == METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT,
            "IndexRecJPQPrune: only METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT is supported");

    const SearchParametersRecJPQPrune* p =
            dynamic_cast<const SearchParametersRecJPQPrune*>(params);
    size_t bs = p ? p->batch_size : batch_size;
    int64_t max_iter = p ? p->max_iterations : max_iterations;
    float infl = p ? p->ub_inflation : ub_inflation;
    bool exact = p ? p->exact_mode : exact_mode;
    RecJPQPruneStats* stats = p ? p->stats : nullptr;

    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(bs >= 1, "batch_size must be >= 1, got %zu", bs);
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(
            infl >= 1.0f, "ub_inflation must be >= 1.0, got %g", (double)infl);
    if (exact) {
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(
                infl == 1.0f,
                "exact_mode requires ub_inflation == 1.0 (got %g)",
                (double)infl);
        max_iter = -1; // unlimited in exact mode
    }

    ThreadState& ts = get_thread_state();

    bool complete = true;
    for (idx_t qi = 0; qi < n; qi++) {
        complete &= search_one(
                x + qi * d,
                k,
                distances + qi * k,
                labels + qi * k,
                bs,
                max_iter,
                infl,
                exact,
                stats,
                ts);
    }
    last_search_complete.store(complete);
}

get_thread_state():

IndexRecJPQPrune::ThreadState& IndexRecJPQPrune::get_thread_state() const {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(thread_state_mutex);
    auto it = thread_states.find(std::this_thread::get_id());
    if (it != thread_states.end()) {
        return *it->second;
    }
    // evict the oldest cached state when the cache grows too large
    size_t cap = 8;
    #ifdef _OPENMP
    cap = std::max<size_t>(8, 2 * (size_t)omp_get_max_threads());
    #endif
    while (thread_states.size() >= cap) {
        thread_states.erase(thread_states.begin());
    }
    auto state = std::make_shared<ThreadState>();
    thread_states.emplace(std::this_thread::get_id(), state);
    return *state;
}

Wait — the eviction while holding the reference: we return *state; the shared_ptr is in the map; the caller holds a reference — if another thread evicts... eviction only happens under the same mutex, and only when inserting a new thread — an existing thread's state can be evicted by a new thread's insertion while the first thread is still using the reference!! That's a use-after-free risk: thread A has ThreadState& ts = get_thread_state(); thread B (a new thread) inserts and evicts A's state → A's reference dangles → crash.

Fix: have the caller hold a shared_ptr, not a reference:

std::shared_ptr<ThreadState> ts = get_thread_state_ptr();

And use ts->.... A reference via shared_ptr is safe: even if the map entry is erased, A's local shared_ptr keeps the state alive.

But — can A's state be evicted while A is between queries? Yes (another new thread comes in and evicts the oldest — possibly A's). A's shared_ptr is still valid → A just uses the (possibly zeroed out?) state — no, eviction doesn't zero it out, it just releases the map's reference. A's state remains intact and consistent (A is the only one using it — no wait, is that true? The state is keyed by thread id; if the thread id gets reused after A's thread dies... std::thread::id is typically reused for new threads (on macOS/Linux, after a thread dies, its id can be reused by a new thread). Then a new thread B2 reusing A's old id would fetch A's old state (visited vector with A's generation). Problem? The generation counter continues from where A left off; visited entries have A's generation values — for B2's first query, gen = A's last gen + 1 → nothing matches → all "new" ✓ correct. Memory-wise: the old visited is just a buffer. Safe. ✓

So: get_thread_state() returns a std::shared_ptr<ThreadState>. The caller: auto ts = get_thread_state(); and ts->S etc.

Next — a potential issue with the visited generation across index rebuilds: if the user reset() + build()s with a larger ntotal, visited grows (new entries zero-initialized) ✓. Generation continues ✓.

void IndexRecJPQPrune::reconstruct_n(idx_t i0, idx_t ni, float* recons) const {
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(i0 >= 0 && i0 + ni <= ntotal);
    for (idx_t i = 0; i < ni; i++) {
        float* r = recons + i * d;
        const uint8_t* c = item_codes.data() + (i0 + i) * M;

                    codebooks.data() + ((m * B + c[m]) * d_split),
                    d_split * sizeof(float));
        }
    }
}

position_of_id:

idx_t IndexRecJPQPrune::position_of_id(idx_t key) const {
    if (ids_sequential) {
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(key >= 0 && key < ntotal, "id %lld out of range", key);
        return key;
    }
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(id_map_mutex);
    if (!id_map_built) {
        id_to_pos.reserve(ids.size());
        for (size_t i = 0; i < ids.size(); i++) id_to_pos[ids[i]] = (idx_t)i;
        // note: duplicate ids → last one wins
        id_map_built = true;
    }
    auto it = id_to_pos.find(key);
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(it != id_to_pos.end(), "unknown id %lld", (long long)key);
    return it->second;
}

Note: duplicate ids — the map keeps the last position. Acceptable and documented (reconstruct for duplicate ids returns one of them).

Hmm, one issue: ids_sequential — if ids are [0,1,2,...] the sequential fast path ✓. If ids are arbitrary → map. But wait: if the ids are sequential and the key is negative → throw ✓.

                "IndexRecJPQPrune: unsupported metric");
        idxr->d_split = idxr->d / idxr->M;
        READ1(idxr->batch_size);
        READ1(idxr->max_iterations);
        READ1(idxr->ub_inflation);
        READ1_BOOL(idxr->exact_mode);
        read_vector(idxr->item_codes, f);
        read_vector(idxr->ids, f);
        read_vector(idxr->codebooks, f);
        read_vector(idxr->invlists.offsets, f);
        read_vector(idxr->invlists.item_ids, f);
        // consistency checks
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(
                idxr->item_codes.size() ==
                        mul_no_overflow((size_t)idxr->ntotal, idxr->M, "item_codes"),
                "IndexRecJPQPrune: item_codes size mismatch");
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(idxr->ids.size() == (size_t)idxr->ntotal);
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(
                idxr->codebooks.size() ==
                        mul_no_overflow(idxr->M * idxr->B, idxr->d_split, "codebooks"),
                "IndexRecJPQPrune: codebooks size mismatch");
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(
                idxr->invlists.offsets.size() == idxr->M * idxr->B + 1);
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(
                idxr->invlists.item_ids.size() ==
                (size_t)idxr->ntotal * idxr->M);
        idxr->ids_sequential = ...; // recompute
        idx = std::move(idxr);
    }

Now — one more important design question: the type of M and B — size_t. The base Index::d is int. OK.

Also, should IndexRecJPQPrune override sa_code_size()? Base returns a throw. Our codes are M bytes. Providing sa_code_size() = M is consistent with the "standalone codec" story. But sa_encode throws (no quantizer), sa_decode = reconstruct_n... the semantics of sa_decode: "decode a set of vectors from codes" — codes in row-major nM → x in nd. That's exactly our decode. And add_sa_codes(n, codes, xids) — "add vectors computed with the standalone codec" — append to the index! This is a natural incremental API.

Should I implement add_sa_codes? It gives a genuine "add" path: append codes (ids optional → sequential from ntotal), rebuild the CSR. Cost: O(N·M) rebuild per append. Let me implement it — it makes the Index interface more complete, and the task says "add / add_with_ids, as appropriate for the selected construction API." With add_sa_codes, "add" is actually supported via the standalone codec interface (the Faiss-idiomatic way for code-native indexes like IndexFlatCodes).

Implementation:

void IndexRecJPQPrune::add_sa_codes(idx_t n, const uint8_t* codes_in, const idx_t* xids) {
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(!codebooks.empty(), "add_sa_codes requires the codebooks; use build() to provide them");
    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(codes_in != nullptr);
    // append
    size_t old = (size_t)ntotal;
    item_codes.insert(item_codes.end(), codes_in, codes_in + n * M);
    if (xids) ids.insert(ids.end(), xids, xids + n);
    else for i in 0..n: ids.push_back(old + i);
    ids_sequential = recompute;
    invlists.build(item_codes.data(), ntotal, M, B);
    ntotal += n;
    invalidate id_map;
}

And sa_code_size() → M; sa_decode(n, bytes, x) → decode. sa_encode → throw (needs a trained quantizer).

Hmm wait — add_sa_codes when ntotal == 0 but codebooks empty: the user has to call build() first. Throw a message. OK.

Actually hmm, let me reconsider: is add_sa_codes worth it? The base Index::add_sa_codes throws by default. IndexFlatCodes overrides it. For our index, it's a ~20-line append + rebuild. Yes, let's do it — it rounds out the "add" story.

And keep add()/add_with_ids() (dense vectors) throwing with a clear message.

/// Verify that the search output matches the exhaustive baseline under the
/// documented tie policy (first-seen wins): check rank-by-rank score
/// agreement, and that each returned id has exactly the expected score.
void expect_matches(const ExhaustiveResult& exp, const float* D, const idx_t* I, idx_t k, const RecJPQData& data);

Hmm — for the tie-tolerant comparison:

  1. For r in 0..k-1: if exp.ids[r] == -1 → I[r] == -1, D[r] == -inf. Otherwise: |D[r] - exp.scores[r]| ≤ tol. And: the exhaustive score of item I[r] == exp.scores[r] (within tol) (i.e., the returned id has the score expected at that rank — it's a valid top-k member).
  2. When there's no tie near the boundary (gap between exp.scores[k-1] and exp.scores[k] (or k==N) is > tol, and no duplicate scores within the top k): require I[r] == exp.ids[r] exactly.

To implement (2) simply: compute the set of all items whose score is within tol of the k-th boundary score; if that set's size == the count of boundary items in the expected top k → ties at the boundary → tolerant; otherwise strict.

More simply: compare the multiset of (score, id): build a map id→exhaustive_score. Then:

  • Check all returned ids have score ≈ D[r] ✓ (always)
  • Check D[r] ≈ exp.scores[r] for all r ✓ (always — the scores at each rank must match)
  • Check the set of returned ids equals the expected set of top-k ids when there are no ties within tol of the boundary: expected set = {ids[0..k-1]}; but when there are ties, the allowed set = items with score > boundary_tol, plus any subset of items with score ≈ boundary.

Let me implement it this way:

// boundary score
float boundary = k <= N ? all_scores_sorted_desc[k-1] : -inf;
bool boundary_ties = exists an item j not in the expected top k with |score(j) - boundary| <= tol;
if (!boundary_ties) { expect exact id match }
else { expect the count of returned ids with score ≈ boundary == the count in the expected top k, and all returned ids above the boundary match exactly }

That's rigorous. all_scores: computed in the exhaustive baseline (N floats) — keep in the result struct for the check.

    # DD mode: link to main faiss library with DD-specific definitions
    # When FAISS_OPT_LEVEL=dd, the main faiss library is built with DD enabled,
    # so we link to faiss (not a separate faiss_dd).
    # FAISS_ENABLE_DD exposes SIMDConfig class to consuming code (e.g., tests)
    # COMPILE_SIMD_* flags enable DD code paths in headers (architecture-specific)
    # Note: No SIMD compile flags here - DD handles dispatch internally.

    #
    # Architecture-specific definitions mirror simd_dispatch.bzl dispatch_config:

    target_compile_definitions(${target} PRIVATE FAISS_ENABLE_DD)

      target_compile_definitions(${target} PRIVATE COMPILE_SIMD_AVX2 COMPILE_SIMD_AVX512)
    elseif(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "(aarch64|arm64|ARM64)")
      target_compile_definitions(${target} PRIVATE COMPILE_SIMD_ARM_NEON)
    endif()
    target_link_libraries(${target} PRIVATE faiss)
  endif()
endfunction()

There are\n * M * B posting lists, identified by\n *\n *     list_id = split * B + sub_item_id\n *\n * The posting list of (split, sub_item_id) contains the internal positions\n * of all items whose code at that split equals sub_item_id.\n *\n * Storage is CSR-style:\n *\n *     offsets has M * B + 1 entries;\n *     the items of list l are item_ids[offsets[l] .. offsets[l + 1]).\n *\n * The storage is dense and unpadded: no slot is reserved for empty posting\n * lists and there is at most one heap allocation for all list contents (and\n * one for the offsets). Within each posting list, item positions appear in\n * ascending order (the order in which items were added), which makes the\n * lists amenable to sequential access.\n */\nstruct RecJPQInvertedLists {\n    size_t M = 0; ///< number of splits\n    size_t B = 0; ///< number of sub-item ids per split\n\n    /** offsets of the M * B + 1 posting list boundaries */\n    std::vector<size_t> offsets;\n    /** concatenation of all posting lists: N * M entries after build */\n    std::vector<idx_t> item_ids;\n\n    /** Two-pass construction from a row-major N x M uint8 code matrix.\n     *\n     * The first pass counts the items per posting list, a prefix sum turns\n     * the counts into offsets and the second pass fills the contiguous\n     * item storage. Item positions are preserved in ascending order.\n     *\n     * @param item_codes  N * M codes, the code at split m of item i is at\n     *                    item_codes[i * M + m], must be in [0, B)\n     * @param N           number of items\n     * @param M           number of splits, >= 1\n     * @param B           number of sub-item ids per split, in [1, 256]\n     */\n    void build(const uint8_t* item_codes, size_t N, size_t M, size_t B);\n\n    /** Drop all postings and metadata. */\n    void clear();\n\n    /// number of items in the posting list (split, sub_item_id)\n    size_t list_size(size_t split, size_t sub_item_id) const;\n\n    /// pointer to the first entry of the posting list (nullptr when the\n    /// list is empty or the lists have not been built)\n    const idx_t* get_list(size_t split, size_t sub_item_id) const;\n\n    /// half-open range [begin, end) of the posting list contents\n    std::pair<const idx_t*, const idx_t*> get_list_range(\n            size_t split,\n            size_t sub_item_id) const;\n\n    /// total number of postings (= N * M after a build)\n    size_t total_entries() const {\n        return item_ids.size();\n    }\n};\n\n} // namespace faiss\n"

i < N; i++) {\n        const uint8_t* c = item_codes + i * M;\n        for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {\n            FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(\n                    c[m] < B,\n                    \"RecJPQInvertedLists: item %\" PRId64\n                    \" has code %u >= B (%zu) in split %zu\",\n                    (idx_t)i,\n                    (unsigned)c[m],\n                    B,\n                    m);\n            offsets[(m * B + c[m]) + 1]++;\n        }\n    }\n    // prefix sum: offsets[l] becomes the start of posting list l\n    for (size_t l = 0; l < nlists; l++) {\n        offsets[l + 1] += offsets[l];\n    }\n\n    // pass 2: fill the contiguous storage, preserving item order\n    item_ids.resize(N * M);\n    std::vector<size_t> cursor(offsets.begin(), offsets.end() - 1);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; i++) {\n        const uint8_t* c = item_codes + i * M;\n        for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {\n            item_ids[cursor[m * B + c[m]]++] = (idx_t)i;\n        }\n    }\n\n    this->M = M;\n    this->B = B;\n}\n\nvoid RecJPQInvertedLists::clear() {\n    offsets.clear();\n    item_ids.clear();\n    M = 0;\n    B = 0;\n}\n\nsize_t RecJPQInvertedLists::list_size(\n        size_t split,\n        size_t sub_item_id) const {\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(split < M);\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(sub_item_id < B);\n    const size_t l = split * B + sub_item_id;\n    return offsets[l + 1] - offsets[l];\n}\n\nconst idx_t* RecJPQInvertedLists::get_list(\n        size_t split,\n        size_t sub_item_id) const {\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(split < M);\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(sub_item_id < B);\n    if (item_ids.empty()) {\n        return nullptr;\n    }\n    return &item_ids[offsets[split * B + sub_item_id]];\n}\n\nstd::pair<const idx_t*, const idx_t*> RecJPQInvertedLists::get_list_range(\n        size_t split,\n        size_t sub_item_id) const {\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(split < M);\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(sub_item_id < B);\n    if (item_ids.empty()) {\n        return {nullptr, nullptr};\n    }\n    const size_t l = split * B + sub_item_id;\n    const idx_t* base = item_ids.data();\n    return {base + offsets[l], base + offsets[l + 1]};\n}\n\n} // namespace faiss\n",

{
  "content": "/*\n * Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates.\n *\n * This source code is licensed under the MIT license found in the\n * LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.\n */\n\n#pragma once\n\n#include <atomic>\n#include <cstddef>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <memory>\n#include <mutex>\n#include <thread>\n#include <unordered_map>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <faiss/Index.h>\n#include <faiss/MetricType.h>\n#include <faiss/invlists/RecJPQInvertedLists.h>\n\nnamespace faiss {\n\n/// Statistics collected during search(), for the caller to inspect.\n/// When several queries are searched in one call, the counters accumulate\n/// over the queries of the call.\nstruct RecJPQPruneStats {\n    /// number of main-loop iterations executed\n    size_t iterations = 0;\n    /// number of unique items whose score was computed\n    size_t items_scored = 0;\n    /// number of posting-list entries visited (before deduplication)\n    size_t postings_traversed = 0;\n    /// number of sub-item ids processed\n    size_t sub_items_processed = 0;\n    /// final value of the sigma upper bound (last query of the call)\n    float final_sigma = 0;\n    /// final value of the theta threshold (last query of the call)\n    float final_theta = 0;\n};\n\n/** Search parameters for IndexRecJPQPrune.\n *\n * Exactness guarantees (see IndexRecJPQPrune::search):\n *  - exact_mode = true (default): the search runs until the exact pruning\n *    condition sigma <= theta holds, so the result is guaranteed to be the\n *    exact top-K under the documented tie-breaking policy. ub_inflation\n *    must be 1.0 and max_iterations is ignored (unlimited).\n *  - exact_mode = false: the search may stop early as soon as\n *    sigma <= theta * ub_inflation (ub_inflation >= 1.0), or after\n *    max_iterations main-loop iterations (>= 0). The result is then only a\n *    best-effort top-K over the items scored so far; check\n *    IndexRecJPQPrune::last_search_complete after the call.\n */\nstruct SearchParametersRecJPQPrune : SearchParameters {\n    /// number of sub-item ids processed per main-loop iteration (BS), >= 1\n    size_t batch_size = 8;\n    /// safety limit on the main-loop iterations; < 0 means unlimited.\n    /// Ignored in exact mode.\n    int64_t max_iterations = -1;\n    /// multiplier applied to the pruning threshold in approximate mode:\n    /// the search stops as soon as sigma <= theta * ub_inflation.\n    /// Must be >= 1.0; 1.0 (default) keeps the search exact.\n    float ub_inflation = 1.0f;\n    /// when true (default), the search runs to exact termination\n    bool exact_mode = true;\n    /// if non-null, filled with the statistics of the search\n    RecJPQPruneStats* stats = nullptr;\n};\n\n/** Index of RecJPQ-compressed item embeddings, searched with the\n * RecJPQPrune dynamic pruning algorithm.\n *\n * Reference: \"Efficient Recommendation with Millions of Items by Dynamic\n * Pruning of Sub-Item Embeddings\", Petrov, Macdonald and Tonellotto,\n * SIGIR 2025 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00560).\n *\n * Each of the N items is represented by M codes in [0, B) (one per split);\n * the item embedding is the concatenation of the M sub-item embeddings\n * looked up from the codebooks G[m][b] in R^d_split, with d_split = d / M.\n * The score of an item for a query phi is the sum over the splits of the\n * dot product of the sub-item embedding with the corresponding sub-query:\n *\n *     score(i) = sum_m S[m][item_codes[i][m]]\n *     S[m][b]  = dot(G[m][b], phi_m)\n *\n * This is the PQTopK scoring function. The search implements Algorithm 1 of\n * the paper: sub-item ids are processed per split in descending order of\n * their S score; at every iteration the split whose next unprocessed\n * sub-item has the highest score contributes a batch of batch_size\n * sub-item ids, whose posting lists yield the candidate items; the new\n * candidates are scored with the S lookup table and merged into a running\n * top-K. The search terminates when the upper bound on the score of any\n * unscored item\n *\n *     sigma = sum_m S[m][Q[m][P[m]]]   (-inf for exhausted splits)\n *\n * drops to the score theta of the K-th best item found so far; under this\n * condition no unscored item can reach the top-K.\n *\n * The index is built from pre-computed codes and codebooks (typically from\n * an existing IndexPQ), not from dense vectors: see build(). add() and\n * add_with_ids() therefore throw; add_sa_codes() accepts RecJPQ codes.\n *\n * Results are returned in descending score order. Ties in score are broken\n * deterministically by discovery order: among items with an equal score,\n * the item that first entered a candidate batch (earlier iteration, then\n * earlier position within the batch) ranks first. This policy makes the\n * pruning condition sigma <= theta exact, since an unscored item tying the\n * threshold necessarily loses the tie-break against an already scored one.\n *\n * Only METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT is supported: higher scores are better.\n *\n * Thread safety: const methods (search, reconstruct, ...) may be called\n * concurrently from several threads; each search thread uses its own\n * scratch buffers, including the deduplication state. Non-const methods\n * (build, reset) must not run concurrently with anything else.\n */\nstruct IndexRecJPQPrune : Index {\n    /// number of splits\n    size_t M = 0;\n    /// number of sub-item ids per split, in [1, 256]\n    size_t B = 0;\n    /// dimensionality of one split (d / M)\n    size_t d_split = 0;\n\n    /** row-major N * M item codes; the code at split m of item i is at\n     * item_codes[i * M + m] */\n    std::vector<uint8_t> item_codes;\n    /** external ids, one per item (size ntotal) */\n    std::vector<idx_t> ids;\n    /** codebooks: G[m][b][j] at codebooks[(m * B + b) * d_split + j] */\n    std::vector<float> codebooks;\n\n    /** CSR inverted lists over the item codes */\n    RecJPQInvertedLists invlists;\n\n    /// default search parameters, used when search() gets no params\n    size_t batch_size = 8;\n    int64_t max_iterations = -1;\n    float ub_inflation = 1.0f;\n    bool exact_mode = true;\n\n    /// true after the most recent search() call ran every query to exact\n    /// termination; false when an approximate stop (ub_inflation > 1.0 or\n    /// the max_iterations limit) triggered first\n    std::atomic<bool> last_search_complete{true};\n\n    /** Construct an empty index.\n     *\n     * @param d      embedding dimension, a positive multiple of M\n     * @param M      number of splits, >= 1\n     * @param B      number of sub-item ids per split, in [1, 256]\n     * @param metric must be METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT\n     */\n    explicit IndexRecJPQPrune(\n            size_t d,\n            size_t M,\n            size_t B,\n            MetricType metric = METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT);\n\n    /** Populate the index from RecJPQ codes and codebooks.\n     *\n     * The index must be empty (call reset() first after a previous build).\n     * The supplied arrays are copied; the caller keeps ownership of them.\n     *\n     * @param n          number of items\n     * @param item_codes N*M uint8 codes, the code at split m of item i at\n     *                   item_codes[i * M + m], each in [0, B)\n     * @param codebooks  M*B*d_split floats, G[m][b][j] at\n     *                   codebooks[(m * B + b) * d_split + j]\n     * @param ids        optional external ids, size n; when null the\n     *                   sequential ids 0..n-1 are used. Duplicate ids are\n     *                   allowed.\n     */\n    void build(\n            size_t n,\n            const uint8_t* item_codes,\n            const float* codebooks,\n            const idx_t* ids = nullptr);\n\n    /** Compute the M x B sub-item score matrix (PQTopK lookup table) for\n     * the query x, row-major: S[m][b] = dot(G[m][b], x[m*d_split..]).\n     * @param S  output, size M * B, caller-allocated\n     */\n    void compute_sub_item_scores(const float* x, float* S) const;\n\n    /** Score a single item with the precomputed sub-item score matrix:\n     * score(i) = sum_m S[m][item_codes[i * M + m]].\n     * @param S  output of compute_sub_item_scores\n     */\n    float score_item(size_t i, const float* S) const;\n\n    /** @param x  dense query vectors, not supported: the index stores\n     *            pre-computed RecJPQ codes, not dense vectors\n     */\n    void add(idx_t n, const float* x) override;\n    void add_with_ids(idx_t n, const float* x, const idx_t* xids) override;\n\n    /** Add items from RecJPQ codes (standalone codec interface).\n     *\n     * The codebooks must already be present (they are set by build()); the\n     * item codes are appended to the index and the inverted lists are\n     * rebuilt over all items, so repeated calls are O(N) each.\n     *\n     * @param codes  n*M uint8 codes, as for build()\n     * @param xids   optional external ids, size n; when null the sequential\n     *               ids ntotal .. ntotal + n - 1 are used\n     */\n    void add_sa_codes(idx_t n, const uint8_t* codes, const idx_t* xids)\n            override;\n\n    /** size of the standalone codec: M bytes per item (one uint8 code per\n     * split) */\n    size_t sa_code_size() const override;\n\n    /** Decode RecJPQ codes back into (approximate) full embeddings.\n     * @param bytes  n*M uint8 codes\n     * @param x      output, size n * d\n     */\n    void sa_decode(idx_t n, const uint8_t* bytes, float* x) const override;\n\n    void search(\n            idx_t n,\n            const float* x,\n            idx_t k,\n            float* distances,\n            idx_t* labels,\n            const SearchParameters* params = nullptr) const override;\n\n    /// drops all items; the codebooks and dimensions are kept\n    void reset() override;\n\n    /** Reconstruct the (approximate) embedding of the item with external\n     * id key. */\n    void reconstruct(idx_t key, float* recons) const override;\n    void reconstruct_batch(\n            idx_t n,\n            const idx_t* keys,\n            float* recons) const override;\n    /** Reconstruct the items with external ids i0 .. i0 + ni - 1\n     * (Faiss convention for external ids). */\n    void reconstruct_n(idx_t i0, idx_t ni, float* recons) const override;\n\n    /** Reconstruct the items at internal positions i0 .. i0 + ni - 1. */\n    void reconstruct_positions(idx_t i0, idx_t ni, float* recons) const;\n\n    /// size in bytes of the index data (codes, ids, codebooks, lists)\n    size_t memory_footprint() const;\n\n    /// index is always \"trained\": it is built from a trained codebook\n    bool is_trained() const {\n        return true;\n    }\n\nprivate:\n    /// per-thread scratch used by search(); never shared between threads\n    struct ThreadState {\n        /// sub-item score matrix, M * B\n        std::vector<float> S;\n        /// sorted sub-item ids per split (descending score), M * B\n        std::vector<uint8_t> Q;\n        /// current position in Q per split, M\n        std::vector<size_t> P;\n        /// scratch for the per-split sub-item id sort\n        std::vector<size_t> order;\n\n        struct Entry {\n            float score;\n            idx_t pos; ///< internal item position\n            uint32_t seq; ///< discovery sequence (tie-break)\n        };\n        /// running top-K result set, sorted by (score desc, seq asc)\n        std::vector<Entry> topk;\n        /// merge buffer: topk union current candidate batch\n        std::vector<Entry> merge;\n        /// candidate batch of the current iteration (internal positions)\n        std::vector<idx_t> cand_pos;\n\n        /// deduplication: visited[pos] is the generation of the last query\n        /// that scored the item at internal position pos\n        std::vector<uint32_t> visited;\n        uint32_t generation = 0;\n    };\n\n    /// scratch of the calling thread, created on first use; the shared_ptr\n    /// keeps the state alive even if the cache evicts it from another thread\n    std::shared_ptr<ThreadState> get_thread_state() const;\n\n    /// run the RecJPQPrune algorithm for one query; returns true when the\n    /// search ran to exact termination\n    bool search_one(\n            const float* xq,\n            idx_t k,\n            float* distances,\n            idx_t* labels,\n            size_t batch_size,\n            int64_t max_iterations,\n            float ub_inflation,\n            bool exact_mode,\n            RecJPQPruneStats* stats,\n            ThreadState& ts) const;\n\n    /// external id -> internal position; throws when the id is unknown\n    idx_t position_of_id(idx_t key) const;\n    /// recompute ids_sequential for the current ids\n    void recompute_ids_sequential();\n\n    mutable std::mutex thread_state_mutex;\n    mutable std::unordered_map<\n            std::thread::id,\n            std::shared_ptr<ThreadState>>\n            thread_states;\n\n    /// lazily built external id -> internal position map (reconstruct)\n    mutable std::mutex id_map_mutex;\n    mutable std::unordered_map<idx_t, idx_t> id_to_pos;\n    mutable bool id_map_built = false;\n    /// true when ids[i] == i for all i\n    bool ids_sequential = true;\n};\n\n} // namespace faiss\n",

The sequence is unique per item within a query, so this\n/// is a total order.\ninline bool entry_before(\n        const IndexRecJPQPrune::ThreadState::Entry& a,\n        const IndexRecJPQPrune::ThreadState::Entry& b) {\n    return a.score > b.score || (a.score == b.score && a.seq < b.seq);\n}\n\n} // namespace\n\nIndexRecJPQPrune::IndexRecJPQPrune(\n        size_t d,\n        size_t M,\n        size_t B,\n        MetricType metric)\n        : Index(d, metric), M(M), B(B) {\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(d > 0, \"IndexRecJPQPrune: d must be > 0\");\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(M > 0, \"IndexRecJPQPrune: M must be > 0\");\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(B >= 1, \"IndexRecJPQPrune: B must be >= 1\");\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(\n            B <= 256,\n            \"IndexRecJPQPrune: B must be <= 256 (item codes are uint8)\");\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(\n            d % M == 0, \"IndexRecJPQPrune: d must be a multiple of M\");\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(\n            metric == METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT,\n            \"IndexRecJPQPrune: only METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT is supported\");\n    d_split = d / M;\n}\n\nvoid IndexRecJPQPrune::recompute_ids_sequential() {\n    ids_sequential = true;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < ids.size(); i++) {\n        if (ids[i] != (idx_t)i) {\n            ids_sequential = false;\n            return;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nvoid IndexRecJPQPrune::build(\n        size_t n,\n        const uint8_t* item_codes,\n        const float* codebooks,\n        const idx_t* ids) {\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(\n            ntotal == 0,\n            \"IndexRecJPQPrune::build: index is not empty; call reset() first\");\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(\n            item_codes != nullptr,\n            \"IndexRecJPQPrune::build: item_codes must not be null\");\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(\n            codebooks != nullptr,\n            \"IndexRecJPQPrune::build: codebooks must not be null\");\n\n    this->item_codes.assign(item_codes, item_codes + n * M);\n    this->codebooks.assign(codebooks, codebooks + M * B * d_split);\n    if (ids != nullptr) {\n        this->ids.assign(ids, ids + n);\n    } else {\n        this->ids.resize(n);\n        std::iota(this->ids.begin(), this->ids.end(), (idx_t)0);\n    }\n    recompute_ids_sequential();\n\n    invlists.build(this->item_codes.data(), n, M, B);\n    ntotal = (idx_t)n;\n\n    {\n        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(id_map_mutex);\n        id_to_pos.clear();\n        id_map_built = false;\n    }\n}\n\nvoid IndexRecJPQPrune::add(idx_t /*n*/, const float* /*x*/) {\n    FAISS_THROW_MSG(\n            \"IndexRecJPQPrune does not support add(): it stores \"\n            \"pre-computed RecJPQ codes, not dense vectors. Build the index \"\n            \"from codes and codebooks with IndexRecJPQPrune::build(), for \"\n            \"example from an existing IndexPQ: codes with pq.compute() and \"\n            \"codebooks with pq.centroids. To append codes use \"\n            \"add_sa_codes().\");\n}\n\nvoid IndexRecJPQPrune::add_with_ids(\n        idx_t /*n*/,\n        const float* /*x*/,\n        const idx_t* /*xids*/) {\n    FAISS_THROW_MSG(\n            \"IndexRecJPQPrune does not support add_with_ids(): it stores \"\n            \"pre-computed RecJPQ codes, not dense vectors. Build the index \"\n            \"with IndexRecJPQPrune::build() or append codes with \"\n            \"add_sa_codes().\");\n}\n\nvoid IndexRecJPQPrune::add_sa_codes(\n        idx_t n,\n        const uint8_t* codes,\n        const idx_t* xids) {\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(codes != nullptr);\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(\n            !codebooks.empty(),\n            \"IndexRecJPQPrune::add_sa_codes: no codebooks; use build() to \"\n            \"construct the index first\");\n\n    const size_t ntotal_old = (size_t)ntotal;\n    item_codes.insert(item_codes.end(), codes, codes + (size_t)n * M);\n    if (xids != nullptr) {\n        ids.insert(ids.end(), xids, xids + n);\n    } else {\n        for (idx_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n            ids.push_back((idx_t)ntotal_old + i);\n        }\n    }\n    recompute_ids_sequential();\n\n    // CSR construction requires all items; rebuild over the whole catalogue\n    invlists.build(item_codes.data(), (size_t)ntotal + n, M, B);\n    ntotal += n;\n\n    {\n        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(id_map_mutex);\n        id_to_pos.clear();\n        id_map_built = false;\n    }\n}\n\nsize_t IndexRecJPQPrune::sa_code_size() const {\n    return M;\n}\n\nvoid IndexRecJPQPrune::sa_decode(\n        idx_t n,\n        const uint8_t* bytes,\n        float* x) const {\n    FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(bytes != nullptr);\n    for (idx_t i = 0; #define READ1(x) READANDCHECK(&(x), 1)

// Reads a single byte into a bool, rejecting any byte that is not the
// canonical encoding for the platform's bool representation. Reading a
// non-canonical byte directly into a bool is undefined behavior and
// trips UBSan's invalid-bool-load check. To stay ABI-portable, we
// assign via the language-defined conversion (b != 0) and then compare
// the resulting bool's storage byte back against the byte we read - the
// roundtrip succeeds iff the input byte was already canonical on this
// platform. FAISS only ever writes the canonical encoding via
// WRITE1(bool), so well-formed indices roundtrip cleanly; corrupt or
// attacker-controlled input that places a non-canonical byte at a bool
// offset is rejected as a FaissException.
#define READ1_BOOL(x)                                                      \
    {                                                                      \
        static_assert(                                                     \
                sizeof(x) == 1, "READ1_BOOL: destination must be 1 byte"); \
        uint8_t b;                                                         \
        READANDCHECK(&b, 1);                                               \
        (x) = (b != 0);                                                    \
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(                                            \
                *reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t*>(&(x)) == b,              \
                "invalid bool encoding 0x%02x for %s",                     \
                b,                                                         \
                #x);                                                       \
    }

#define READ1_DUMMY(x_type) \
    {                       \
        x_type x = {};      \
        READ1(x);           \
    }

// Rejects vectors whose total allocation would exceed the configurable
// byte limit (default 1 TB).
#define READVECTOR(vec)                                                  \
    {                                                                    \
        size_t size;                                                     \
        READANDCHECK(&size, 1);                                          \
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(                                              \
                size >= 0 &&                                             \
                size < (faiss::get_deserialization_vector_byte_limit() / \
                        sizeof(*(vec).data())));                         \
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(                                          \
                size <= SIZE_MAX / sizeof((vec)[0]),                     \
                "READVECTOR: size %zu would overflow for element "       \
                "size %zu",                                              \
                size,                                                    \
                sizeof((vec)[0]));                                       \
        (vec).resize(size);                                              \
        READANDCHECK((vec).data(), size);                                \
    }

#define WRITEANDCHECK(ptr, n)                         \
    {                                                 \
        size_t ret = (*f)(ptr, sizeof(*(ptr)), n);    \
        FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(                       \
                ret == (n),                           \
                "write error in %s: %zd != %zd (%s)", \
                f->name.c_str(),                      \
                ret,                                  \
                size_t(n),                            \

Main helpers:

struct RecJPQData {
    size_t M, B, d_split, N;
    std::vector<uint8_t> codes;   // N*M
    std::vector<float> codebooks; // M*B*d_split
    std::vector<idx_t> ids;
};

RecJPQData make_recjpq(
    size_t M, size_t B, size_t d_split, size_t N, uint32_t seed,
    std::function<idx_t(size_t)> id_of = nullptr) {
    std::mt19937 rng(seed);
    std::uniform_int_distribution<int> subid(0, (int)B - 1);
    std::normal_distribution<float> gauss(0.0f, 1.0f);
    RecJPQData data;
    data.M = M; data.B = B; data.d_split = d_split; data.N = N;
    data.codes.resize(N * M);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; i++)
        for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++)
            data.codes[i * M + m] = (uint8_t)subid(rng);
    data.codebooks.resize(M * B * d_split);
    for (auto& v : data.codebooks) v = gauss(rng);
    data.ids.resize(N);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; i++) data.ids[i] = id_of ? id_of(i) : (idx_t)i;
    return data;
}

IndexRecJPQPrune make_index(const RecJPQData& data, bool with_ids = true) {
    IndexRecJPQPrune idx(data.M * data.d_split, data.M, data.B);
    idx.build(
        data.N, data.codes.data(), data.codebooks.data(),
        with_ids ? data.ids.data() : nullptr);
    return idx;  // hmm — move semantics: the class is moveable (default move constructor: mutex is non-movable!).
}

Problem: the class contains std::mutex → the default move constructor is deleted → the class is non-movable! make_index which returns by value won't compile. Need to return a unique_ptr, or construct in place. Let's return std::unique_ptr<IndexRecJPQPrune>.

Exhaustive baseline:

struct Exhaustive {
    std::vector<float> all_scores; // N, item i at all_scores[i]
    std::vector<idx_t> top_ids;    // k, -1 padded
    std::vector<float> top_scores; // k, -inf padded
    std::vector<float> sorted_scores; // N scores sorted descending
};

Exhaustive exhaustive_topk(const RecJPQData& data, const float* phi, idx_t k) {
    const size_t d = data.M * data.d_split;
    std::vector<float> S(data.M * data.B);
    // compute S manually: dot(codebooks[m][b], phi[m*ds..])
    for (m) for (b) for (j) S[m*B+b] += codebooks[(m*B+b)*ds+j] * phi[m*ds+j];
    std::vector<float> scores(data.N);
    for (i) for (m) scores[i] += S[m*B + codes[i*M+m]];
    // sort indices by (score desc, pos asc)
    std::vector<size_t> order(data.N);
    iota...
    sort(order, [scores](a,b){ return scores[a]>scores[b] || (scores[a]==scores[b] && a<b); });
    ...
}

Comparison helper:

// Tolerance relative to float32 computation
float score_tol() { return 1e-4f; }

bool score_eq(float a, float b) {
    float tol = 1e-4f * std::max({1.f, std::fabs(a), std::fabs(b)});
    return std::fabs(a - b) <= tol;
}

void check_results(
    const Exhaustive& exp,
    const RecJPQData& data,
    const float* D,
    const idx_t* I,
    idx_t k) {
    const size_t N = data.N;
    // 1) each returned entry must have the expected score and a valid id
    for (idx_t r = 0; r < k; r++) {
        if (r >= N) {
            EXPECT_EQ(I[r], -1);
            EXPECT_EQ(D[r], -inf);
            continue;
        }
        // rank-r score must match
        ASSERT_TRUE(score_eq(D[r], exp.top_scores[r])) ...;
        // id must be valid and its exhaustive score must equal D[r]
        idx_t id = I[r];
        int pos = data.ids_to_pos... (map id->pos; in the test we know the ids)
        ASSERT_TRUE(pos >= 0);
        EXPECT_TRUE(score_eq(D[r], exp.all_scores[pos]));
    }
    // 2) strict id match when there are no ties at the boundary
    if (k <= (idx_t)N) {
        float boundary = exp.top_scores[k - 1];
        // number of items with score within tol of the boundary
        size_t n_boundary = count over all N: |all_scores[i] - boundary| <= tol;
        size_t boundary_in_topk = count over r<k: score_eq(exp.top_scores[r], boundary);
        if (n_boundary == boundary_in_topk) {
            // no ties straddling the boundary: ids must match exactly
            for (r < min(k,N)) EXPECT_EQ(I[r], exp.top_ids[r]);
        }
    }
}

Hmm wait, about the "no ties" determination: if all items within tol of the boundary are already in the expected top k, then any exact top-K implementation must return exactly the expected ids. Otherwise, a tolerant check suffices.

Note on expected top_ids: my baseline sorts by (score desc, pos asc) — this is a "reference" ordering that differs from the index's discovery-order tie policy only when there are ties. When there are no ties, both orderings coincide on the top k set and the order. ✓

Edge: k > N → top_ids padded with -1.

That's 6 configs × 5 queries × ~5 k × 6 bs = 900 searches on small data — fine for a unit test (each search on 2000 items is trivial).

For the negative-scores test: scale the query by -1 and… actually more simply: codebooks ~ N(0,1) random; pick a query and its negation → scores flip sign. Compare both against the exhaustive (which handles it naturally). Do: data with a mostly positive codebook (codebooks[i] = |gauss|), query negative → mostly negative scores. Compare against exhaustive.

All-equal-scores test: zero query → all scores 0. k=10: expect 10 distinct ids, all score 0, determinism across runs, and last_search_complete is true. Also verify that the returned ids are all valid.

M=1 test: M=1, B=8, ds=8, N=300 → compare against exhaustive.
B=1 test: B=1 → all items have the same score (all codes are 0) → tie case; k=100<N: expect 100 distinct ids, all equal scores, complete.

Empty posting lists: covered by random data with B > N (config {8, 32, 16, 2000}: 32 lists per split, average 62 → not empty… use config {4, 64, 8, 200}: 256 lists, 800 postings → many empty ✓). Let's add {4, 64, 8, 200, 7}.

Clone test similarly.

Now — an important detail in the comparison: my index's search returns scores as float (the sum of S lookups); the exhaustive baseline computes S with the same float operations but in a different order (my gemv vs. the test's naive loop) → small fp differences. The 1e-4 relative tolerance handles it.

Also, let me think about the deterministic mstar tie-break: my loop uses if (s > best) → the first (smallest m) wins on ties ✓ deterministic.

And the Q sort tie-break: (score desc, sub-id asc) ✓ deterministic.

Candidate encounter order: sub-item j in j0..j1 order (descending S within the split), then list order (ascending pos). Deterministic ✓.

Now let's write the test file.

Also — regarding EXPECT and ASSERT in the helper check_results — use EXPECT_* (non-fatal) so all mismatches get reported; the function is called per case. Use ADD_FAILURE for setup problems.

One more design point for the test: data.ids_to_pos — a helper to map an external id to an internal position for the check: build an unordered_map in the test data struct (for unique ids); for the duplicate-id test, the map holds one of them — handle separately there.

Objective

Implement RecJPQPrune (Petrov et al., SIGIR 2025, arXiv:2505.00560) as a native Faiss index faiss::IndexRecJPQPrune in /Users/craig.macdonald/git/faiss (Faiss 1.16.0-dev), with CSR inverted lists, exact top-K search via the paper's Algorithm 1, unit tests, benchmarks, build integration, a demo, and documentation. All changes so far are uncommitted.

Requirements

  • Derive IndexRecJPQPrune directly from faiss::Index (NOT IndexFlatCodes/IndexIVF); METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT only; higher scores better; results descending score; pad missing with -inf/-1.
  • Data model: N×M uint8 codes (B ≤ 256, documented), codebooks [M][B][ds] with ds = d/M, arbitrary int64 external IDs, internal positions in [0,N).
  • Dedicated CSR inverted lists class RecJPQInvertedLists (two-pass build, no padding, no per-list allocations, build/list_size/get_list/get_list_range).
  • Scoring: precompute S[m][b] = dot(codebooks[m][b], phi_m) once per query; item score = sum_m S[m][codes[i][m]] (PQTopK lookup, no full dot products during search).
  • Exact pruning: default exact mode (ub_inflation=1.0, no arbitrary iteration cap, no early termination, sigma ≤ theta condition), handle negatives/empty lists/BS>B; document a deterministic tie policy; report incompleteness if max_iterations hit.
  • Dedup via uint32 generation counter (never shared between concurrent searches); thread-safe concurrent search().
  • Construction API: IndexRecJPQPrune(d, M, B) + build(n, item_codes, codebooks, ids=nullptr); no need for full embeddings; clear ownership (data copied).
  • Deliverables: .h/.cpp for index and inverted lists, unit tests, benchmark executable, CMake integration, minimal C++ example, documentation. Before finishing: run Faiss tests + new tests, verify exact equivalence vs exhaustive PQTopK, report deviations + benchmark/memory results.
  • No GPU, no advanced SIMD (future work).

Decisions

  • Construction via build(); add()/add_with_ids() throw with informative messages; add_sa_codes() supported (append codes, rebuild CSR, O(N) per call); sa_code_size()=M, sa_decode() implemented.
  • Tie policy (documented in header): ties broken by discovery order (first-seen wins); Q[m] sorted by (score desc, sub-item id asc); argmax m* ties → lowest m; makes σ ≤ θ termination exact.
  • Top-K merge: per-iteration std::partial_sort of union (current topK ∪ new candidates) with unique per-query seq counter; theta = k-th score when k items collected else -inf.
  • Per-thread scratch via std::unordered_map<std::thread::id, std::shared_ptr<ThreadState>> under mutex with bounded cache (max(8, 2×omp threads)); caller keeps shared_ptr for lifetime safety; visited generation counter with overflow wrap (clear + restart at gen 1).
  • S matrix computed with M cblas_sgemv calls (CblasRowMajor, m=B, n=d_split), matching ProductQuantizer::compute_LUT pattern.
  • last_search_complete is std::atomic<bool>; stats via caller-owned RecJPQPruneStats* in SearchParametersRecJPQPrune {batch_size=8, max_iterations=-1, ub_inflation=1.0f, exact_mode=true, stats}.
  • IO: fourcc "IRJQ" in write/read; clone: custom branch in Cloner::clone_Index rebuilding via build() (class non-copyable due to mutex); default constructor for read_index.
  • reconstruct* use external-id semantics (Faiss convention); reconstruct_positions() added for internal positions; lazy id_to_pos unordered_map under mutex, fast path when ids_sequential (public data member).
  • Build env (no system cmake/OpenMP): conda env at /private/var/folders/14/c1q7fktj67n_msjy_m0bhjl00000gp/T/opencode/faiss-build (cmake, ninja, clang, llvm-openmp, openblas, gflags); compiler $ENV/bin/clang++-23.

72: /** Index of RecJPQ-compressed item embeddings, searched with the
73:  * RecJPQPrune dynamic pruning algorithm.
74:  *
75:  * Reference: "Efficient Recommendation with Millions of Items by Dynamic
76:  * Pruning of Sub-Item Embeddings", Petrov, Macdonald and Tonellotto,
77:  * SIGIR 2025 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00560).
78:  *
79:  * Each of the N items is represented by M codes in [0, B) (one per split);
80:  * the item embedding is the concatenation of the M sub-item embeddings
81:  * looked up from the codebooks G[m][b] in R^d_split, with d_split = d / M.
82:  * The score of an item for a query phi is the sum over the splits of the
83:  * dot product of the sub-item embedding with the corresponding sub-query:
84:  *
85:  *     score(i) = sum_m S[m][item_codes[i][m]]
86:  *     S[m][b]  = dot(G[m][b], phi_m)
87:  *
88:  * This is the PQTopK scoring function. The search implements Algorithm 1 of
89:  * the paper: sub-item ids are processed per split in descending order of
90:  * their S score; at every iteration the split whose next unprocessed
91:  * sub-item has the highest score contributes a batch of batch_size
92:  * sub-item ids, whose posting lists yield the candidate items; the new
93:  * candidates are scored with the S lookup table and merged into a running
94:  * top-K. The search terminates when the upper bound on the score of any
95:  * unscored item
96:  *
97:  *     sigma = sum_m S[m][Q[m][P[m]]]   (-inf for exhausted splits)
98:  *
99:  * drops to the score theta of the K-th best item found so far; under this
100:  * condition no unscored item can reach the top-K.
101:  *
102:  * The index is built from pre-computed codes and codebooks (typically from
103:  * an existing IndexPQ), not from dense vectors: see build(). add() and
104:  * add_with_ids() therefore throw; add_sa_codes() accepts RecJPQ codes.
105:  *
106:  * Results are returned in descending score order. Ties in score are broken
107:  * deterministically by discovery order: among items with an equal score,
108:  * the item that first entered a candidate batch (earlier iteration, then
109:  * earlier position within the batch) ranks first. This policy makes the
110:  * pruning condition sigma <= theta exact, since an unscored item tying the
111:  * threshold necessarily loses the tie-break against an already scored one.
112:  *
113:  * Only METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT is supported: higher scores are better.
114:  *
115:  * Thread safety: const methods (search, reconstruct, ...) may be called
116:  * concurrently from several threads; each search thread uses its own
117:  * scratch buffers, including the deduplication state. Non-const methods
118:  * (build, reset) must not run concurrently with anything else.
119:  */

220:     // short-lived threads are evicted (their state is re-created on demand)

233: bool IndexRecJPQPrune::search_one(
234:         const float* xq,
235:         idx_t k,
236:         float* distances,
237:         idx_t* labels,
238:         size_t batch_size,
239:         int64_t max_iterations,
240:         float ub_inflation,
241:         bool exact_mode,
242:         RecJPQPruneStats* stats,
243:         ThreadState& ts) const {
244:     // pad the outputs (missing results are -inf / -1)
245:     std::fill(labels, labels + k, -1);
246:     std::fill(distances, distances + k, kNegInf);
247:     if (k <= 0 || ntotal == 0) {
248:         return true;
249:     }
250: 
251:     // ---- 1. sub-item score matrix (PQTopK lookup table), once per query
252:     const size_t nb = M * B;
253:     if (ts.S.size() < nb) {
254:         ts.S.resize(nb);
255:     }
256:     compute_sub_item_scores(xq, ts.S.data());
257: 
258:     // ---- 2. per split, sort the sub-item ids by descending score
259:     // (ties: lower sub-item id first, for determinism)
260:     if (ts.Q.size() < nb) {
261:         ts.Q.resize(nb);
262:     }
263:     if (ts.P.size() < M) {
264:         ts.P.resize(M);
265:     }
266:     if (ts.order.size() < B) {
267:         ts.order.resize(B);
268:     }
269:     for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {
270:         std::iota(ts.order.begin(), ts.order.begin() + B, (size_t)0);
271:         const float* Sm = ts.S.data() + m * B;
272:         std::sort(
273:                 ts.order.begin(),
274:                 ts.order.begin() + B,
275:                 [Sm](size_t a, size_t b) {
276:                     return Sm[a] > Sm[b] || (Sm[a] == Sm[b] && a < b);
277:                 });
278:         for (size_t j = 0; j < B; j++) {
279:             ts.Q[m * B + j] = (uint8_t)ts.order[j];
280:         }
281:         ts.P[m] = 0;
282:     }
283: 
284:     // ---- 3. initial upper bound: sigma = sum of the best unprocessed
285:     // sub-item score of every split
286:     float sigma = 0.f;
287:     for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {
288:         sigma += ts.S[m * B + ts.Q[m * B]];
289:     }
290:     // threshold: score of the K-th best item so far (-inf while < K scored)
291:     float theta = kNegInf;
292: 
293:     // ---- 4. deduplication generation for this query
294:     if (ts.visited.size() < (size_t)ntotal) {
295:         ts.visited.resize((size_t)ntotal, 0);
296:     }
297:     if (ts.generation == std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max()) {
298:         // counter overflow: clear the table and restart at generation 1
299:         std::fill(ts.visited.begin(), ts.visited.end(), 0);
300:         ts.generation = 0;
301:     }
302:     const uint32_t gen = ++ts.generation;
303:     uint32_t seq = 0; ///< discovery sequence counter for this query
304: 
305:     // ---- main iteration (Algorithm 1 of Petrov et al., SIGIR 2025)
306:     int64_t iter = 0;
307:     size_t items_scored = 0;
308:     size_t postings_traversed = 0;
309:     size_t sub_items_processed = 0;
310:     bool capped = false;
311: 
312:     while (sigma > theta) {
313:         if (items_scored >= (size_t)ntotal) {
314:             break; // every item is scored: the top-K is final
315:         }
316:         if (max_iterations >= 0 && iter >= max_iterations) {
317:             capped = true;
318:             break;
319:         }
320: 
321:         // (1) split whose next unprocessed sub-item scores highest
322:         // (ties: lowest split first, for determinism)
323:         int mstar = -1;
324:         float best = kNegInf;
325:         for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {
326:             if (ts.P[m] >= B) {
327:                 continue; // split exhausted
328:             }
329:             const float s = ts.S[m * B + ts.Q[m * B + ts.P[m]]];
330:             if (s > best) {
331:                 best = s;
332:                 mstar = (int)m;
333:             }
334:         }
335:         if (mstar < 0) {
336:             break; // all splits exhausted (sigma is -inf then)
337:         }
338: 
339:         // (2) next batch of sub-item ids from that split, clamped at B
340:         const size_t j0 = ts.P[mstar];
341:         const size_t j1 = std::min(B, j0 + batch_size);
342: 
343:         // (3) candidates = union of the posting lists of the batch,
344:         // deduplicated by internal position
345:         ts.cand_pos.clear();
346:         for (size_t j = j0; j < j1; j++) {

348:             const auto range = invlists.get_list_range((size_t)mstar, sub);

353:                 if (ts.visited[p] != gen) {
354:                     ts.visited[p] = gen;
355:                     ts.cand_pos.push_back(p);
356:                 }
357:             }
358:             postings_traversed += (size_t)(end - begin);
359:         }
360:         sub_items_processed += j1 - j0;
361: 
362:         // (4) score the new candidates with the S lookup table (PQTopK)
363:         const size_t nnew = ts.cand_pos.size();
364:         if (nnew > 0) {
365:             ts.merge.clear();
366:             ts.merge.reserve(ts.topk.size() + nnew);
367:             ts.merge.insert(
368:                     ts.merge.end(), ts.topk.begin(), ts.topk.end());
369:             for (size_t t = 0; t < nnew; t++) {
370:                 const uint8_t* c = item_codes.data() + (size_t)ts.cand_pos[t] * M;
371:                 float s = 0.f;
372:                 for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {
373:                     s += ts.S[m * B + c[m]];
374:                 }
375:                 ts.merge.push_back(ThreadState::Entry{s, ts.cand_pos[t], ++seq});
376:             }
377: 
378:             // (5) keep the top min(k, |union|) under (score desc, seq asc);
379:             // the first-seen-wins tie policy falls out of the unique seq
380:             const size_t keep =
381:                     std::min<size_t>((size_t)k, ts.merge.size());
382:             std::partial_sort(
383:                     ts.merge.begin(),
384:                     ts.merge.begin() + keep,
385:                     ts.merge.end(),
386:                     entry_before);
387:             ts.topk.assign(ts.merge.begin(), ts.merge.begin() + keep);
388: 
389:             // (6) threshold = score of the K-th best item (if K known)
390:             theta = (ts.topk.size() == (size_t)k)
391:                     ? ts.topk.back().score
392:                     : kNegInf;
393:             items_scored += nnew;
394:         }
395: 
396:         // (7) advance the pointer and recompute the upper bound
397:         ts.P[mstar] = j1;
398:         sigma = 0.f;
399:         for (size_t m = 0; m < M; m++) {
400:             if (ts.P[m] >= B) {
401:                 sigma = kNegInf;
402:                 break;
403:             }
404:             sigma += ts.S[m * B + ts.Q[m * B + ts.P[m]]];
405:         }
406: 
407:         iter++;
408:     }
409: 
410:     // ---- output, in descending score order (topk is already sorted)
411:     const size_t out = std::min<size_t>((size_t)k, ts.topk.size());
412:     for (size_t r = 0; r < out; r++) {
413:         distances[r] = ts.topk[r].score;
414:         labels[r] = ids[ts.topk[r].pos];
415:     }
416: 
417:     if (stats != nullptr) {
418:         stats->iterations += (size_t)iter;
419:         stats->items_scored += items_scored;
420:         stats->postings_traversed += postings_traversed;
421:         stats->sub_items_processed += sub_items_processed;
422:         stats->final_sigma = sigma;
423:         stats->final_theta = theta;
424:     }
425: 
426:     return !capped;
427: }

429: void IndexRecJPQPrune::search(
430:         idx_t n,
431:         const float* x,
432:         idx_t k,
433:         float* distances,
434:         idx_t* labels,
435:         const SearchParameters* params) const {
436:     FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT(k >= 0);
437:     FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_MSG(
438:             metric_type == METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT,
439:             "IndexRecJPQPrune: only METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT is supported");
440: 
441:     const SearchParametersRecJPQPrune* p =
442:             dynamic_cast<const SearchParametersRecJPQPrune*>(params);
443:     const size_t bs = p ? p->batch_size : batch_size;
444:     int64_t max_iter = p ? p->max_iterations : max_iterations;
445:     const float infl = p ? p->ub_inflation : ub_inflation;
446:     const bool exact = p ? p->exact_mode : exact_mode;
447:     RecJPQPruneStats* stats = p ? p->stats : nullptr;
448: 
449:     FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(bs >= 1, "batch_size must be >= 1 (got %zu)", bs);
450:     FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(
451:             infl >= 1.0f,
452:             "ub_inflation must be >= 1.0 (got %g)",
453:             (double)infl);
454:     if (exact) {
455:         FAISS_THROW_IF_NOT_FMT(
456:                 infl == 1.0f,
457:                 "exact_mode requires ub_inflation == 1.0 (got %g)",
458:                 (double)infl);
459:         max_iter = -1; // unlimited in exact mode
460:     }
461: 
462:     auto ts = get_thread_state();
463: 
464:     bool complete = true;
465:     for (idx_t qi = 0; qi < n; qi++) {
466:         complete &= search_one(
467:                 x + (size_t)qi * d,
468:                 k,
469:                 distances + (size_t)qi * k,
470:                 labels + (size_t)qi * k,
471:                 bs,
472:                 max_iter,
473:                 infl,
474:                 exact,
475:                 stats,
476:                 *ts);
477:     }
478:     last_search_complete.store(complete);
479: }
